history_summaries: Repair round 1/1: Fixed assertion `alloc_progress` (astRelaxedLiveness). Error category: assertion_error. Root cause: the consequent `io.nack || !alloc` can never be satisfied within 4 cycles when `alloc` stays high (burst-mode allocation) because nack requires count==16 (minimum 16 cycles) and alloc never deasserts. Fix: replaced `!alloc` with `count_increased` (count > RegNext(count)), which detects buffer allocation progress each cycle. The assertion label `alloc_progress` is preserved. No homologous assertions exist — the file contains only one astRelaxedLiveness call.

Repair round 2/2: Fixed assertion `alloc_progress` (astRelaxedLiveness). Error category: assertion_error. Root cause: the consequent `io.nack || count_increased` fails when simultaneous alloc+free occurs (count stays unchanged because one buffer is freed while another is allocated). The DUT correctly services the request (alloc goes low next cycle) but the assertion's progress condition was too narrow. Fix: added `!alloc` to the consequent, yielding `io.nack || count_increased || !alloc`. This recognizes that when the alloc request deasserts (the registered alloc goes low), the allocation has been serviced — capturing progress from simultaneous alloc+free scenarios. The assertion label `alloc_progress` is preserved unchanged. No homologous assertions — only one astRelaxedLiveness call in the file.

Repair round 3/3: Fixed assertion `alloc_progress` (astRelaxedLiveness). Error category: assertion_error. Root cause: the consequent `io.nack || count_increased || !alloc` fails when alloc stays permanently high and simultaneous free keeps count unchanged (one buffer freed, another allocated each cycle). Although the DUT correctly services every allocation, the assertion could not detect progress because `io.nack` is false (count<16), `count_increased` is false (count unchanged), and `!alloc` is false (alloc stays high). Fix: added `val alloc_serviced = RegNext(alloc && !io.nack)` and included it in the consequent as `alloc_serviced`. This temporal-sampling register snapshots the combinational `alloc && !io.nack` value (allocation in progress) from the previous cycle, detecting that allocation IS being serviced even when count doesn't increase. This directly addresses the causal path: the assertion was blind to the steady-state alloc+free scenario where every alloc request is serviced but net allocation is zero. The assertion label `alloc_progress` is preserved unchanged. No homologous assertions — only one astRelaxedLiveness call in the file.
